etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English celer, seler, from Anglo-Norman celer, Old French celier (modern cellier), from Late Latin cellārium, from Latin cella. Doublet of cellarium.

definitions.definition: An enclosed underground space, often under a building, used for storage or shelter.
A wine collection, especially when stored in a cellar.
(slang) Last place in a league or competition.

quote.citation: 2008 June 25, Lucy Burningham, “Beer Lovers Make Room for Brews Worth a Wait”, in New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: Mr. VandenBerghe says he’s cellared such memorable bottles as the Batch 1 Adam from Hair of the Dog, a 14-year-old ale from Portland, Ore., that’s 10 percent alcohol, and the Trappistes Rochefort 10, a Quadrupel Belgian ale that peaks around age 10.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From 15th century English saler, from French salière, from Latin salarius (“relating to salt”), from Latin sal (“salt”).

definitions.definition: (historical) A small dish for holding salt.
